Through: Mr.Ambuj Chauhan, Advo
 petitioners.
 versus
 State Govt. Of N.C.T. Delhi & Anr.

Through: Mr.Sunil Kumar Gautam,
 State with SI Rahu  Mr.Parveen Kumar, 
 with R2/complainan  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE YOGESH KHANNA  ORDER % 15.02.2023 1.

Petitioners file this petition for quashing of the FIR No.273/2021 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act registered at police station Seemapuri, Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 22.10.2014 according to Muslim rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
No child is born from this wedlock.

However, due to matrimonial discord, the couple started living separately from each other since 29.09.2019 and on the complaint of respondent No.2 aforesaid FIR was registered against the petitioners.
During the pendency of proceedings, the couple have settled the matter per settlement agreement dated 16.08.2022 before the Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.
The parties have also obtained divorce by executing the Talaknama thrice on 06.10.2022; 11.11.2022; and 21.12.2022 respectively.

Pursuant to settlement, the petitioner No.1 has agreed to pay Rs.3.90 Lacs to respondent No.2 towards all her claims of alimony, maintenance - past, present and future,
stridhan, and dowry articles etc.

The entire settled amount has already been paid to respondent No.2.
3.

The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has received the settled amount of Rs.3.90 Lacs from petitioner No.1 and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

sentences.text: Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has received the settled amount from the petitioners.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
5. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

Consequently, FIR No.273/2021 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act registered at police station Seemapuri, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
FEBRUARY 15, 2023
